validity.population: one synthetic nanodevice, one homogeneous extracellular compartment, and one homogeneous cellular sink
validity.physiological_state: software verification only; no physiological state
validity.description: An M5.5 threshold event activates irreversible first-order payload release followed by irreversible first-order cellular uptake.

sources.citation: Wendt, Regine (2024), Einsatz von Nanotechnologien in der Praezisionsmedizin, Sections 4.4-4.5 and 5.4
sources.role: nanodevice activation, localized release, uptake, and cell-response vision

sources.citation: MEHLISSA Next M5.5 intracellular response network
sources.role: typed threshold event and source identity

sources.citation: MEHLISSA Next ADR-0039 conservative nanodevice release and uptake
sources.role: ownership, analytical chain, and validity boundary

limitations: The drug identity, payload, device, rates, amount, compartment semantics, and trigger are synthetic software-test values.
Release and uptake are irreversible homogeneous first-order processes with no diffusion distance, binding, saturation, metabolism, or elimination.
The intracellular threshold is used as an abstract activation decision and does not establish a physical cell-to-device signaling mechanism.
Intracellular drug amount is inventory only and does not yet alter the M5.5 reaction network or cause apoptosis.
The reference verifies conservation and analytical kinetics, not efficacy, dose, toxicity, safety, or clinical validity.
